notes.title: Colonize 0.2 is live - Now with cows and sheeps!
notes.content:
Hello, fellow Colonizers; we are pushing a Major update, many fixes, and some new buildings and decorations! Thanks to our community and kudos to our community beta testers - the doctor, Lisek, Rezler, Umar, FastDepp, S.N.A.F.U.


Added cows!
https://i.postimg.cc/FK5S1Z3n/cowshed.png
Added sheep!
https://i.postimg.cc/3Jk0B6Zc/sheepfold.png
Added squares, small and tall flags
https://i.postimg.cc/dQHTGvGC/square.png
Added gates for the fences!
https://i.postimg.cc/kG46LhPD/fences.png
We have added the palisade and palisade gate. 
Now, it is always open, but it will be changed so that a player can choose an open or closed state.
https://i.postimg.cc/KjPGqPR4/palisades.png
Added + and - to each building
You can choose the maximum amount for storage in the buildings - for example, you can turn off the firewood creation for one sawmill and open it for another.
https://i.postimg.cc/fL5S2QF6/plusminus.png

Other fixes & improvements:

 Changed UI scale in the game - now it should not scale uniformly
 Added brightness and contrast
 The language settings are saved only after confirmation
 Trees are saved even while they are being chopped down and will reappear in the exact location
 The amount of wood obtained from a tree depends on the tree's height
 If one resource output is full, the production will switch to the second output until it is also full
 The woodcutter's tree-finding algorithm has been improved to prioritize the nearest trees
 After saving and loading, people's positions on benches are retained. The same applies to the Hunter, who previously behaved strangely
 The bakery now correctly shows when it is in operation
 We completely reworked the save system, which should fix most of the problems
 Eating House has more storage for meat, fish, potatoes
 Change default time for warehouse, eating house, cellar, and woodcutter
 General optimization improved, turning off some cast shadows for small objects and rocks
 Fixed - #1986 - After manually switching innkeeper, he tends to get stuck there
 Fixed - #1985 - Clicking on the bottom of the screen will move you to the map too
 Fixed - #1894 - Children grown-up has the same clothes
 Fixed - #1941 - Saving takes a too-long time
 Fixed - #1952 - Wrong sitting point on one bench
 Fixed - #1987 - Inn doors are opening in opposite directions
 Fixed - #2005 - Bakery Light on off 
 Fixed - #2011 - Change the sound of the children's audio
 Fixed - #2018 - Residents often forget to eat despite being in the Eating House building

notes.content:
New Features and Improvements:


 Childbirth: Families will have a more balanced mix of boys and girls.
 Adjusted Eating: Citizens prioritize eating based on their hunger levels. For instance, they will consume eggs before meat when they are less hungry.
 New Statistics Window: Access detailed population statistics with the newly added window.
 Added Languages: Polish and Simplified Chinese languages are now available.
 Improved Route Searching (Navmesh): Route searching and road updates are now up to 200% faster in some cases.
 Population Window Hide: When clicking on a humanoid, the population window will automatically hide.
 Bakery, Public Shelter, and Cellar Lights and Window Adjustments: Lighting and window adjustments have been made to enhance visual clarity.
 Rock Small Collider: Small colliders have been removed from small rocks to facilitate smoother road creation.
 Smoke Adjustment: Smoke effects have been fine-tuned for improved visual aesthetics.
 RIP Meshes without Grass: Rest in Peace (RIP) Meshes no longer feature grass for better consistency.


This update enhances lighting, collision detection, visual effects, and language options, providing an enriched gameplay experience. Additionally, RIP meshes have been updated for better consistency and immersion.

notes.title: Colonize 0.1.7.0
notes.content:
Colonize Version 0.1.7: Explore the Latest Updates!

Colonizers,

We're thrilled to announce the release of Colonize version 0.1.7, bringing many exciting new features and improvements to enhance your gaming experience. Let's dive in:

New Features:


 Fences: Four new types of wooden fences enhance your colony's aesthetics and structure, providing new landscaping possibilities.
 Revamped Building Menu Icons: The building menu now has a fresh look and all-new icons, making navigation and selection easier than ever.
 Audio for Door Opening: Immerse yourself further into the world of Colonize with added audio effects when doors are opened, enhancing gameplay immersion.
 Redesigned Building Menu: When placing buildings, enjoy a redesigned menu interface that provides a more intuitive and user-friendly experience.
 Illustrated Load Sockets: Visualize your colony's functionality with added visual illustrations to load sockets, improving clarity and aesthetics.


Bug Fixes and Improvements:


 Corrected camera positioning for a better view at the start of the game.
 Adjusted citizen attributes for smoother interactions and gameplay mechanics.
 Implemented minor bug fixes to enhance game stability and performance.



Thank you for your continued support and feedback as we strive to make Colonize the best it can be. Happy colonizing!

notes.title: Colonize 0.1.6
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow Colonizers! We're thrilled to present to you our latest substantial update!


 Livestock Sustainability: Pigs and Chickens now have increased longevity without food.
 Work Experience: All professions now utilize experience gained at work.
 Enhanced Visuals: Added vibrant Citizen illustrations.
 Improved Interface: Citizens now feature three tabs for better organization.
 Access to Colonize Wiki: Explore the inaugural version of the Colonize wiki via the Menu.
 Refined Audio Mixing: Experience superior audio quality with enhanced mix levels.
 Snowscape Optimization: Resolved a bug affecting trees in snowy areas.
 Introduction of Firewood: Essential addition for heating and cooking purposes.
 Lush Grasslands: Grass now appears denser with tile-based rendering across all maps.
 Loading Screen: Enjoy a loading screen while the game initializes.
 Streamlined Features: Winter Clothes removed for a smoother gameplay experience.
 Cellar Functionality: The cellar no longer collects water from the Well.
 Performance Enhancements: Enjoy a 10-15fps improvement for smoother gameplay.
 Auditory Feedback: Added clicking sounds to all buttons for better user experience.
 UI Polishing: Corrected padding issues in the settings menu.
 Ship Renaming: Harbor name changed to Trade Ship for accuracy.
 Seasonal Wardrobe: Clothes now automatically switch to winter attire.
 Road Connectivity: Roads now snap into place after loading.
 Inn Consumption: Increased food consumption rate in the Inn.
 Storage Adjustments: Cellar storage limits revised for certain resources.
 Birth Rate Control: Added a slider for controlling house population growth.
 Expanded Audio Library: Additional sound effects for various buildings.
 Annual Immigration: Expect new arrivals every January if shelter space is available.
 Bakery Automation: The bakery now autonomously receives water.
 Informative Notifications: Receive alerts for restricted building areas or insufficient food for livestock.
 Tutorial Enhancement: Bug fixed regarding tab selection in the tutorial.
 Walking Speed Correction: Resolved issue with walking speed at maximum velocity.
 Improved Stability: Enjoy smoother FPS performance with over 200 citizens.
 Seasonal Farming: Farmers refrain from planting seeds when temperatures drop below 8 degrees Celsius.


In addition, numerous minor updates and tweaks have been implemented for an even more immersive experience!

notes.title: DevBlog #05 - Level Design
notes.content:
Most of our level consists of trees, bushes, and nature in general. Today it is no longer possible to know how it once looked or what exactly made up nature in the past. That's why we start from today's maps and where the forests could have been 400 years ago.

What is the purpose of the shader in the level design process?

Shaders define materials' properties, such as color, texture, transparency, and reflectivity. They also control how light interacts with these materials. Shaders can be customized using Unity's Shader Graph visual interface or by writing code in the ShaderLab language.

https://i.postimg.cc/Vk08WG0j/Screenshot-119.png

Our Terrain shader combines several different types of surfaces, from beaches and different types of grass to mountains. Added to this is the possibility for snow through various pre-prepared masks or masks produced in real-time in the shader. You can see on the right side all the inputs that go into the shader for a terrain, masks, tiled textures, and some floats that control the shader behavior.

If we have everything ready and are satisfied with the terrain, we will proceed to the actual painting of the objects, scattering. We have several types of trees, shrubs, almost 100 different stones, and forest debris.
https://i.postimg.cc/fR1w4nQ2/Screenshot-118.png

Everything is manually placed on a 1x1km field. One level took us over two months, and three artists were involved in the level design. We currently have three maps ready, which we are still satisfied with. We want at least six levels prepared for you when the game is released.

notes.title: Why We Still Haven't Finished Our Game
notes.content:
Making a video game is a complex and time-consuming process that requires a lot of work, creativity, and dedication. Despite our best efforts, it's common for game development projects to run over schedule.

As many of you guys wrote us, the first quarter of 2023 is almost over. Where is the game?

One of the most common reasons game development projects go off track is scope creep. This refers to the gradual expansion of the project's goals and requirements, increasing workload and development time. Sometimes, new ideas or features are added to the game that was not originally planned, or existing features are expanded upon. While this can lead to a better game overall, it can also cause delays and make it difficult to reach the finish line.

That is one of our problems, but the most significant problem is planning or even planning with people. A human being frequently wants free time, vacations, or getting sick. Something that needed to be clarified for me when planning all the features and creating a schedule. 

Now the game is in the phase where all the art is almost done, and the rule 80/20 is now present. What does it mean? That 80 percent of work requires the same amount of time to complete the rest of the 20 percent of the task/game. To be more specific, we started building the Colonize from scratch. We are now in the phase of putting everything together but adding all the ideas, the stuff that worked, and getting rid of the stuff that didn't work in Colonize Prologue.

My idea was simply to show the programmers, ok, here is the game. Make it the same but better, add a save feature, localizations, make the roads, etc. Well, they showed me I was wrong.

But don't worry; we changed the release date to TBA, something we should did in the first place. It does not mean it will take a year or two to make it available, or even the Colonize will be abandoned. Not at all! 

It means we don't want to stress our team and mislead our players.

Best to you all,
- sanchez

notes.title: DevBlog #03 - Terrain Creation
notes.content:
We want the Colonize game to have accurate maps, authentic scenery, trees, animals, mountains, meadows, and everything as it was in the 17th century. We try to get as close to it as possible, so we make each map according to the elevation map of the given area.

Let's show you how we created the Roanoke map!

The environment of the first Roanoke Colony, located on Roanoke Island off the coast of North Carolina, was a mix of coastal plains, forests, and wetlands. The region was also known for having abundant resources, such as timber and fertile soil, which helped the colony establish itself.

We chose a part of Roanoke Island, specifically around the city of Fort Raleigh. Currently, you can see that there is an airport, and the overall development of the given area is relatively large. Almost most of the land is already in use. That's why we had to invent a little and adapt the terrain to our needs.

https://i.postimg.cc/VsVmqJ6T/google-roanoke.jpg

As for technical restrictions, the terrain must be 1x1km in size, have a maximum height of 30-35m, and the construction area of the land is 1m above sea level and must be completely flat. That's why we had to re-engage some semi-automatic processes in the Houdini program, which we already introduced last time.

For input, you have raw data, mostly in poor quality, but they serve well. The data goes through several changes, adding various noise displacements, adjusting the beaches, defining the constructible surface, and meeting all the technical conditions mentioned above. 

https://i.postimg.cc/Sx04PHcf/ronaoke-houdini.jpg

Next, painting the required masks for the shader to create the final appearance in Unity is necessary, but more on that later.

notes.title: DevBlog #01
notes.content:
As promised, we are starting a DevBlog, so you can see how the Colonize is being done! Let us get into it, and the first blog is about buildings, which are essential for every building game, right?

What is the process of creating buildings?

First, we have to find the proper references. We use books and, of course, the Internet, and we think about how they might have looked then. Many buildings still standing from the 16th century have already been reconstructed.

We also have to look at the aesthetics of the buildings. Of course, we want the game to be faithful, but at the same time, we want to satisfy our artistic hearts and the players. Above all, buildings must be beautiful!

The building model goes through several rounds of comments until we get to something we like, and it makes sense for a potential resident or worker. We are trying to think how the building would be built by someone who will use it regularly. Does he want stairs there? Does it need windows? Does it need a place to store raw materials?

If the building is finished, the next part comes where we have to make 10-15 levels of how the building is being built, which is quite laborious and lengthy work. If we have at least 30 buildings in the game, then we must create at least 300 models, which requires strong nerves and a lot of patience.

https://i.postimg.cc/Hn1bp9KB/devblog01c.jpg

Then comes the automation of some extra steps in Houdini, which we'll talk about next time!

Cheers
--sanchez--

notes.title: Base Builder Fest DEMO
notes.content:
Welcome to the next stage of our Colonize game development!


We know that we last communicated with our fans long ago, and here is why, and at the same time, with this blog, we want to show the future of the Colonize game.

First, we are releasing the Colonize Demo game under the main page. It is the same game from the Colonize Prologue page. Why is that so?

The answer is that we are a small indie team with a lot of experience but without a previously published game. Therefore, releasing the Colonize Prologue version of the game was a condition for further funding of the project. This was, of course, very successful and, at the same time, convinced our distributor to invest in us and trust us.

But at one point, we had to decide what to do next, and we dug through the whole game from the basics, so we stopped and concentrated on development. Of course, this did not allow us to develop the Colonize demo or Colonize Prologue game further. So we decided to offer it on the main page and demo to make ourselves visible in the upcoming event, Base Builder Fest.

I hope we have made it clear enough, and at the same time, we promise that we will contact you more regularly in the form of blogs on STEAM as we continue with the game.

Thank you for being so supportive!
